QuestionText: The United Nations was founded in:
Topic: General Knowledge - World Affairs and Current Events
Explanation: The United Nations (UN) was established on October 24, 1945 (now celebrated as UN Day) after World War II, replacing the League of Nations. Originally 51 founding member states; now 193 members. Headquarters: New York City, USA. Six principal organs: General Assembly (all members), Security Council (5 permanent members with veto power: USA, UK, France, Russia, China), Secretariat (Secretary-General), International Court of Justice, Economic and Social Council, Trusteeship Council. Current UN Secretary-General: António Guterres (Portugal, since 2017).

QuestionText: Which international body sets global trade rules?
Options: A) IMF
B) World Bank
C) WTO
D) OPEC
Topic: General Knowledge - World Affairs and Current Events
Explanation: WTO (World Trade Organization): international body governing rules of global trade between nations. Founded January 1, 1995, replacing GATT (General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade). 164 member countries. Functions: negotiating trade agreements, resolving trade disputes, monitoring national trade policies, technical assistance to developing countries. Headquarters: Geneva, Switzerland. India is a founding WTO member. Key issues: agricultural subsidies, intellectual property, digital trade, tariff reductions.

QuestionText: The G20 is a group of:
Options: A) The 20 poorest nations seeking development aid
B) 19 major economies plus the EU, accounting for ~85% of global GDP
C) 20 military superpowers forming a defence alliance
D) 20 nations with the largest populations
Topic: General Knowledge - World Affairs and Current Events
Explanation: G20 (Group of Twenty): forum of 19 major economies + European Union. Members include: USA, China, India, Germany, UK, France, Japan, Russia, Brazil, Australia, Canada, South Korea, Italy, Mexico, Saudi Arabia, South Africa, Turkey, Argentina, Indonesia. Collectively: ~85% of world GDP, 75% of global trade, 67% of world population. India held G20 Presidency in 2023 (New Delhi Summit, September 2023). Focus: global financial stability, economic cooperation, climate change, SDGs.

QuestionText: What is NATO?
Options: A) North Atlantic Trade Organisation
B) North Atlantic Treaty Organization — a military alliance of 32 countries
C) National Alliance for Trade and Oil
D) North American Technology Organisation
Topic: General Knowledge - World Affairs and Current Events
Explanation: NATO (North Atlantic Treaty Organization): military alliance established April 4, 1949. Originally 12 members; now 32 (Sweden joined 2024). Based on collective defence principle (Article 5): an attack on one member is an attack on all. Headquarters: Brussels, Belgium. Supreme Allied Commander Europe (SACEUR) is always an American general. Finland joined in 2023, Sweden in 2024 following Russia's invasion of Ukraine (2022). India is NOT a NATO member — India maintains strategic autonomy and is part of QUAD (with USA, Japan, Australia).

QuestionText: What is the BRICS group?
Options: A) A trade agreement between border countries
B) An alliance of emerging economies: Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa (expanded in 2024)
C) A financial institution for developing nations
D) An environmental treaty among tropical countries
Topic: General Knowledge - World Affairs and Current Events
Explanation: BRICS: originally coined by Goldman Sachs economist Jim O'Neill (2001). Formal grouping: Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa. BRICS nations: ~26% of world's land, ~42% of population, ~26% of global GDP. 2024 expansion: Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, UAE, Saudi Arabia joined as full members — becoming BRICS+. Represent the rising power of the Global South and developing world. New Development Bank (NDB): BRICS-founded multilateral development bank, headquartered in Shanghai. India's PM Modi hosted BRICS Summit 2021.

QuestionText: The SDGs (Sustainable Development Goals) were adopted by:
Options: A) WHO in 2010
B) UN in 2015 as part of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development
C) G7 nations in 2012
D) World Bank in 2000
Topic: General Knowledge - World Affairs and Current Events
Explanation: SDGs (Sustainable Development Goals): 17 goals adopted by all 193 UN member nations in September 2015 as the '2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development.' Replace Millennium Development Goals (MDGs, 2000-2015). 17 goals, 169 targets covering: No Poverty, Zero Hunger, Good Health, Quality Education, Gender Equality, Clean Water, Clean Energy, Decent Work, Climate Action, Peace and Justice, etc. India is committed to achieving SDGs. Progress monitoring by UN DESA (Department of Economic and Social Affairs).

QuestionText: Which country has the largest army in the world?
Options: A) USA
B) Russia
C) India
D) China
Topic: General Knowledge - World Affairs and Current Events
Explanation: China has the world's largest active military force (People's Liberation Army/PLA) with approximately 2 million active personnel. India ranks 2nd (~1.45 million), USA 3rd (~1.4 million), North Korea (~1.28 million), Russia (~1 million). However, USA has the largest defence budget (~$800+ billion). Military power rankings consider: technology, nuclear weapons, naval power, air force, training, global projection capability — not just personnel numbers. USA is often ranked most powerful overall despite smaller numbers.

QuestionText: The Paris Agreement of 2015 deals with:
Options: A) Nuclear weapons reduction
B) Climate change — limiting global temperature rise to 1.5-2°C above pre-industrial levels
C) International trade liberalisation
D) Refugee rights and immigration
Topic: General Knowledge - World Affairs and Current Events
Explanation: Paris Agreement (COP21): landmark international climate treaty adopted December 12, 2015, in Paris. 196 parties (countries). Key goals: Limit global temperature rise to 'well below 2°C' (ideally 1.5°C) above pre-industrial levels. Achieve net-zero emissions by second half of 21st century. NDCs (Nationally Determined Contributions): each country sets its own emission reduction targets. India's NDCs: 45% emission intensity reduction by 2030, 50% electricity from renewables by 2030, net-zero by 2070. USA withdrew (Trump 2017), rejoined (Biden 2021).

QuestionText: What is the QUAD (Quadrilateral Security Dialogue)?
Options: A) A trade group of four Pacific nations
B) An informal strategic partnership between India, USA, Japan, and Australia focusing on Indo-Pacific security
C) Four-nation nuclear disarmament agreement
D) A four-country climate change alliance
Topic: General Knowledge - World Affairs and Current Events
Explanation: QUAD (Quadrilateral Security Dialogue): informal strategic forum between India, USA, Japan, and Australia. Originally formed 2007, relaunched 2017, upgraded to leader-level summits 2021. Focus: free and open Indo-Pacific, maritime security, COVID-19 vaccines (QUAD Vaccine Partnership), cybersecurity, climate change, critical technologies. Seen as counter to China's growing influence in Indo-Pacific. India maintains strategic autonomy — QUAD is not a military alliance (unlike NATO). First QUAD Summit hosted by US President Biden in Washington DC (2021).

QuestionText: Which country is the world's largest democracy?
Options: A) USA
B) India
C) Brazil
D) Indonesia
Topic: General Knowledge - World Affairs and Current Events
Explanation: India is the world's largest democracy by eligible voter population. 2024 Indian General Election: approximately 968 million eligible voters — the largest electorate in world history. India holds elections across 543 constituencies over several phases. Election Commission of India (ECI) is the independent constitutional body conducting elections. USA is the oldest continuous major democracy (since 1789). India, as both the most populous nation and a functioning democracy since 1952, is often called the 'Mother of Democracy' and 'the world's largest democracy.'

QuestionText: What happened in India on August 15, 1947?
Options: A) India became a Republic
B) India gained independence from British rule
C) The Indian Constitution was adopted
D) India joined the United Nations
Topic: General Knowledge - World Affairs and Current Events
Explanation: August 15, 1947: India gained independence from British colonial rule after 200 years. PM Jawaharlal Nehru gave the historic 'Tryst with Destiny' speech at midnight. India was partitioned into two nations: India and Pakistan (Muslim-majority areas). Boundary Commission headed by Cyril Radcliffe. Partition caused massive displacement (~14 million people) and communal violence. India became a Republic on January 26, 1950 (Constitution Day/Republic Day) — that's when the Indian Constitution came into effect.

QuestionText: The Cold War was primarily between:
Options: A) India and Pakistan
B) USA and USSR (Soviet Union)
C) Germany and Britain
D) China and Japan
Topic: General Knowledge - World Affairs and Current Events
Explanation: Cold War (1947-1991): ideological, political, and economic conflict between USA (capitalism, liberal democracy) and USSR/Soviet Union (communism). 'Cold' because the two superpowers never directly fought each other (feared nuclear war — Mutually Assured Destruction). Proxy wars fought in Korea (1950-53), Vietnam (1955-75), Afghanistan (1979-89). Ended with USSR collapse (1991). India followed Non-Aligned Movement (NAM) — didn't join either bloc. Arms race, Space Race, Berlin Wall (1961-1989), Cuban Missile Crisis (1962) were Cold War highlights.

QuestionText: What is the International Monetary Fund (IMF)?
Options: A) A bank that gives loans to the world's poorest people
B) An international organisation promoting global monetary cooperation, financial stability, and economic growth
C) A fund managed by multinational corporations
D) A currency exchange marketplace
Topic: General Knowledge - World Affairs and Current Events
Explanation: IMF (International Monetary Fund): created 1944 (Bretton Woods Conference), operational 1945. 190 member countries. Functions: promotes monetary cooperation and exchange rate stability, facilitates international trade, provides financial assistance to countries facing economic crises (loans with conditions), economic surveillance and forecasting (World Economic Outlook reports), technical assistance and training. Headquarters: Washington D.C., USA. India has borrowed from IMF (1991 economic crisis — opened India's liberalisation). Managing Director: Kristalina Georgieva (Bulgaria).

QuestionText: Who was the first Secretary-General of the United Nations?
Options: A) Dag Hammarskjöld
B) U Thant
C) Trygve Lie
D) Kurt Waldheim
Topic: General Knowledge - World Affairs and Current Events
Explanation: Trygve Lie of Norway was the first UN Secretary-General (1946-1952). Subsequent SGs: Dag Hammarskjöld (Sweden, 1953-1961 — died in plane crash in Africa), U Thant (Myanmar/Burma, 1961-1971 — first non-European SG), Kurt Waldheim (Austria), Javier Pérez de Cuéllar (Peru), Boutros Boutros-Ghali (Egypt — first African SG), Kofi Annan (Ghana, won Nobel Peace Prize), Ban Ki-moon (South Korea), António Guterres (Portugal, current — since 2017).

QuestionText: What is the significance of January 26 in India?
Options: A) Independence Day
B) Republic Day — the Indian Constitution came into effect in 1950
C) Gandhi Jayanti
D) Martyrs' Day
Topic: General Knowledge - World Affairs and Current Events
Explanation: January 26, 1950: India's Constitution came into force, making India a sovereign democratic republic. Celebrated as Republic Day. The Constitution replaced the Government of India Act 1935 (British law). Dr. B.R. Ambedkar was the chief architect of the Indian Constitution. The Republic Day Parade at Kartavya Path (formerly Rajpath), New Delhi, features military displays, cultural tableaux from states, and a foreign dignitary as chief guest. India chose January 26 as the date because the Indian National Congress had declared Purna Swaraj (complete independence) on January 26, 1930.

QuestionText: Which country hosted the 2022 FIFA World Cup?
Options: A) Russia
B) Brazil
C) Qatar
D) France
Topic: General Knowledge - World Affairs and Current Events
Explanation: The 2022 FIFA World Cup was hosted by Qatar (November 20 – December 18, 2022) — the first World Cup in the Middle East. Argentina won the tournament (beat France in the final on penalties), with Lionel Messi winning his first World Cup. Held in winter (November-December) instead of the usual June-July due to Qatar's extreme summer heat. All eight stadiums were within a 75km radius — smallest World Cup footprint. Qatar controversially won the hosting rights — first time the tournament was held in a Muslim-majority country.

QuestionText: What is the ASEAN grouping?
Options: A) African Strategic Economic Alliance Network
B) Association of Southeast Asian Nations — 10-country economic and political organisation
C) Asian Scientific and Environmental Alliance Network
D) Asian Students Exchange Alliance Network
Topic: General Knowledge - World Affairs and Current Events
Explanation: ASEAN (Association of Southeast Asian Nations): founded August 8, 1967 (Thailand, Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines, Singapore). Now 10 members: + Brunei, Vietnam, Laos, Myanmar, Cambodia. Collective: 660 million people, ~$3.3 trillion GDP (5th largest economy). Headquarters: Jakarta, Indonesia. Focus: economic integration, regional peace, political cooperation. ASEAN Free Trade Area (AFTA): low tariffs among members. India has ASEAN Free Trade Agreement. India-ASEAN summit held annually. ASEAN+3: includes China, Japan, South Korea.

QuestionText: The Nobel Peace Prize for 2014 was jointly awarded to:
Options: A) Malala Yousafzai and Kailash Satyarthi
B) Amartya Sen and Mother Teresa
C) Rajiv Gandhi and Nelson Mandela
D) Rabindranath Tagore and APJ Abdul Kalam
Topic: General Knowledge - World Affairs and Current Events
Explanation: The 2014 Nobel Peace Prize was jointly awarded to Malala Yousafzai (Pakistan, age 17 — youngest Nobel laureate ever) for education rights activism after surviving Taliban assassination attempt, and Kailash Satyarthi (India) for his campaign against child labour (Bachpan Bachao Andolan — Save Childhood Movement). Indian Nobel Peace Prize winners: Mother Teresa (1979), Kailash Satyarthi (2014). Indian Nobel Prize winners in other fields: Rabindranath Tagore (Literature, 1913), C.V. Raman (Physics, 1930), Amartya Sen (Economics, 1998), Abhijit Banerjee (Economics, 2019).

QuestionText: What is the SCO (Shanghai Cooperation Organisation)?
Options: A) A technology cooperation forum for Shanghai-based companies
B) A Eurasian political, economic, and security organisation with India, China, Russia, Pakistan as members
C) A scientific organisation for space cooperation
D) A trade agreement among coastal nations
Topic: General Knowledge - World Affairs and Current Events
Explanation: SCO (Shanghai Cooperation Organisation): founded 2001 (Shanghai). Members: China, Russia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Uzbekistan, India (2017), Pakistan (2017), Iran (2023), Belarus (2024). Covers 40% of world's population, 25% of global GDP. Focus: political, economic, security cooperation, counter-terrorism, regional stability. Headquarters: Beijing, China. Significance for India: despite India-China tensions, India participates for regional stability and engagement with Central Asia. India hosted SCO Summit 2023 (virtual format). Russia-India-China (RIC) trilateral within SCO is significant.

QuestionText: What event is remembered as '9/11'?
Options: A) The fall of the Berlin Wall
B) Terrorist attacks on USA on September 11, 2001 by Al-Qaeda
C) The first atomic bomb dropped on Hiroshima
D) The end of the Cold War
Topic: General Knowledge - World Affairs and Current Events
Explanation: September 11, 2001 (9/11): Al-Qaeda terrorists hijacked four commercial aircraft — two crashed into the World Trade Center towers (New York, both collapsed), one into the Pentagon (Washington), one into a Pennsylvania field (passengers resisted). ~3,000 killed. Led to: US War on Terror, invasion of Afghanistan (2001), invasion of Iraq (2003), creation of Department of Homeland Security, TSA (airport security), enhanced surveillance laws (Patriot Act). Osama bin Laden (Al-Qaeda leader) killed by US Navy SEALs in Pakistan, May 2, 2011.

QuestionText: Assertion: India's Non-Aligned Movement (NAM) policy during the Cold War was a strategic choice. Reason: Staying out of both US and USSR blocs allowed India to receive aid from both sides while maintaining sovereign foreign policy. Which is correct?
Options: A) Both assertion and reason are true; reason correctly explains assertion
B) Both true but reason does not explain assertion
C) Assertion true; reason false
D) Both false
Topic: General Knowledge - World Affairs and Current Events
Explanation: Assertion TRUE: NAM was strategic, not passive. PM Nehru co-founded NAM with Yugoslavia's Tito, Egypt's Nasser, Ghana's Nkrumah, and Indonesia's Sukarno (1961 Belgrade Summit). Reason TRUE and correctly explains: India received economic/military aid from both USA (food aid) and USSR (military equipment, factories like Bhilai Steel Plant) while maintaining independent foreign policy. India could criticise apartheid, colonialism, and military blocs freely. Non-aligned status gave India moral authority and diplomatic flexibility during the Cold War era.

QuestionText: Which Indian astronaut became the first Indian to travel to space?
Options: A) Sunita Williams
B) Rakesh Sharma
C) Kalpana Chawla
D) Satish Dhawan
Topic: General Knowledge - World Affairs and Current Events
Explanation: Rakesh Sharma was the first Indian citizen to travel to space, flying aboard Soviet Soyuz T-11 on April 2, 1984. He spent 7 days 21 hours aboard the Salyut 7 space station. When PM Indira Gandhi asked how India looks from space, he responded 'Saare Jahan Se Accha' ('Better than the entire world' — famous Urdu poem). Kalpana Chawla was the first person of Indian origin (but US citizen) in space (1997), died in Columbia disaster (2003). Sunita Williams is also of Indian heritage and a US astronaut. India's Gaganyaan programme aims for an Indian crewed spaceflight.

QuestionText: What is the ICC (International Cricket Council)?
Options: A) Indian Commerce Council
B) The global governing body for international cricket
C) International Communication Committee
D) Inter-Continental Cricket Club
Topic: General Knowledge - World Affairs and Current Events
Explanation: ICC (International Cricket Council): global governing body for cricket. Headquarters: Dubai, UAE. Founded 1909 (as Imperial Cricket Conference). Members: 108 nations. Organises: Cricket World Cup (ODI — last: India 2023, winner: Australia), T20 World Cup (last: West Indies/USA 2024), ICC Championships, Test match schedules. India is the most powerful member — BCCI (Board of Control for Cricket in India) generates ~70% of global cricket revenue. India won ICC ODI World Cup 1983, 2011, and ICC Champions Trophy 2013.

QuestionText: Which global organisation promotes health worldwide?
Options: A) UNICEF
B) UNESCO
C) WHO
D) UNDP
Topic: General Knowledge - World Affairs and Current Events
Explanation: WHO (World Health Organization): UN agency responsible for international public health. Founded April 7, 1948 (World Health Day). 194 member countries. Headquarters: Geneva, Switzerland. Director-General: Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus (Ethiopia, since 2017). Key work: eradicating diseases (smallpox eradicated 1980), COVID-19 pandemic response, fighting tuberculosis, malaria, HIV/AIDS, setting international health standards. UNICEF: children's welfare. UNESCO: education, science, culture. UNDP: development programmes. UNFCCC: climate change.

QuestionText: What is the Artemis Programme?
Options: A) An EU space programme for Mars exploration
B) NASA-led international programme to return humans to the Moon
C) A European weather satellite network
D) An Indian-US joint venture for space tourism
Topic: General Knowledge - World Affairs and Current Events
Explanation: Artemis Programme: NASA-led international lunar exploration programme aiming to return humans to the Moon (including the first woman and first person of colour). Artemis I: unmanned test (November 2022 — successful). Artemis II: crewed flyby (planned 2025). Artemis III: first crewed lunar landing since Apollo 17 (1972). Partners: ESA (Europe), JAXA (Japan), CSA (Canada), UK. India signed the Artemis Accords in 2023 — a set of principles for peaceful, cooperative space exploration. Gateway: lunar space station planned as part of Artemis infrastructure.

QuestionText: What is the Belt and Road Initiative (BRI)?
Options: A) A road safety campaign by the WHO
B) China's massive infrastructure and investment programme spanning 60+ countries
C) An EU trade route development project
D) A military alliance along China's border
Topic: General Knowledge - World Affairs and Current Events
Explanation: Belt and Road Initiative (BRI): China's massive global infrastructure investment strategy announced by President Xi Jinping in 2013. Involves financing and building roads, railways, ports, pipelines, and digital infrastructure across 60+ countries in Asia, Africa, Europe, and Latin America. Investment: $1+ trillion. Concerns: 'debt trap diplomacy' — some countries (Sri Lanka, Zambia) unable to repay loans, giving China strategic leverage. India has NOT joined BRI — objects to the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) passing through Pakistan-Occupied Kashmir (POK).

QuestionText: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR) was adopted in:
Topic: General Knowledge - World Affairs and Current Events
Explanation: UDHR (Universal Declaration of Human Rights): adopted by UN General Assembly on December 10, 1948 (Human Rights Day). Drafted by commission chaired by Eleanor Roosevelt. 30 articles covering: right to life, liberty, education, fair trial, freedom of speech, assembly, religion, equal rights regardless of race/gender/nationality. Not legally binding (a declaration, not a treaty) but profoundly influential on international law, national constitutions (including India's), and human rights standards. Translated into 500+ languages — most translated document in the world.

QuestionText: Which country has hosted the Olympic Games the maximum number of times?
Options: A) France
B) USA
C) UK
D) Germany
Topic: General Knowledge - World Affairs and Current Events
Explanation: USA has hosted the Olympics the most times: Summer Olympics: St. Louis (1904), Los Angeles (1932, 1984, 2028), Atlanta (1996) = 5 times. Winter Olympics: Squaw Valley (1960), Lake Placid (1932, 1980), Salt Lake City (2002) = 4 times. Total: 9 times. UK and France have each hosted 3 Summer Olympics. India has never hosted the Olympics. India's best Olympic performance: 7 medals at Tokyo 2020 (2021) including Neeraj Chopra's gold in javelin (India's first athletics gold). Paris 2024 Olympics: India won 6 medals including Neeraj Chopra's silver.

QuestionText: What is 'climate change' and who is primarily responsible for it?
Options: A) Natural seasonal weather changes
B) Long-term shifts in global temperature and weather patterns, primarily caused by human greenhouse gas emissions since industrialisation
C) Changes in ocean tides caused by moon
D) Short-term weather events like hurricanes
Topic: General Knowledge - World Affairs and Current Events
Explanation: Climate change: long-term shifts in global temperatures and weather patterns. Since the 1800s, human activities (primarily burning fossil fuels — coal, oil, gas) have released greenhouse gases (CO₂, methane, nitrous oxide), trapping heat in Earth's atmosphere. Effects: rising temperatures, melting ice caps, rising sea levels, extreme weather events (floods, droughts, wildfires). IPCC (Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change) provides scientific consensus. Limiting temperature rise to 1.5°C requires halving global emissions by 2030. Developing countries like India are most vulnerable despite contributing least historically.

QuestionText: Assertion: India's G20 Presidency in 2023 was significant for India's global standing. Reason: India used the Presidency to champion the Global South's concerns and achieved the AU's inclusion as G20 member. Which is correct?
Options: A) Both assertion and reason are true; reason correctly explains assertion
B) Both true but reason does not explain assertion
C) Assertion true; reason false
D) Both false
Topic: General Knowledge - World Affairs and Current Events
Explanation: Assertion TRUE: India's G20 Presidency (December 2022-November 2023) was a diplomatic triumph, holding 200+ events across India. Reason TRUE and correctly explains: India successfully pushed for African Union (AU — 55 African nations) to become G20's 21st member (announced at New Delhi Summit). Theme: 'Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam' (the world is one family). India highlighted Global South priorities: food security, climate finance, debt relief, digital public infrastructure. The New Delhi Declaration was adopted by consensus despite Russia-Ukraine geopolitical tensions — a major diplomatic achievement.

QuestionText: What is ISRO?
Options: A) Indian Space Research Organisation — India's national space agency
B) International Space Research Organisation
C) Indian Science Research Organisation
D) Indo-Soviet Research Operations
Topic: General Knowledge - World Affairs and Current Events
Explanation: ISRO (Indian Space Research Organisation): India's national space agency, founded August 15, 1969. Headquarters: Bengaluru. Chairman: reports to PM. Key achievements: Chandrayaan-1 (2008 — discovered water on Moon), Mangalyaan/Mars Orbiter Mission (2014 — Asia's first Mars mission, first attempt success), Chandrayaan-3 (2023 — first soft landing near Moon's south pole), GSLV, PSLV launch vehicles, NavIC (India's GPS), 100+ satellites of 34 countries launched. India's space programme is one of the world's most cost-effective. Gaganyaan: India's first crewed space mission (in development).

QuestionText: Which country has the highest number of UNESCO World Heritage Sites?
Options: A) India
B) China
C) Italy
D) France
Topic: General Knowledge - World Affairs and Current Events
Explanation: Italy has the most UNESCO World Heritage Sites with 58 (as of 2023). China: 57, Germany: 52, France: 52, Spain: 50. India: 42 (as of 2023) including Taj Mahal, Ajanta & Ellora Caves, Red Fort, Qutb Minar complex, Western Ghats, Sundarbans, Khajuraho Temples, Hampi, Mahabodhi Temple. Hoysala temples and Shantiniketan were added in 2023. UNESCO World Heritage Sites are designated for outstanding universal value. India's latest addition: Hoysala temples (Karnataka) in 2023.

QuestionText: What is the significance of Chandrayaan-3 in 2023?
Options: A) First Indian crewed lunar mission
B) India became the fourth country and first to soft-land near the Moon's south pole
C) India's first Mars orbiter spacecraft
D) India's first satellite launched from Moon's orbit
Topic: General Knowledge - World Affairs and Current Events
Explanation: Chandrayaan-3 (August 23, 2023): India's Vikram lander successfully soft-landed near the Moon's south pole — a world first. India became only the 4th country to land on the Moon (after USSR, USA, China). The landing site was named 'Shiv Shakti Point' by PM Modi. Pragyan rover deployed, conducted experiments, detected sulphur and other elements. Mission lasted ~14 Earth days (one lunar day). Cost: ~₹615 crore ($74 million) — remarkably cost-effective. India lost Chandrayaan-2 lander in 2019. Chandrayaan-3's success was a historic achievement for India's space programme.

QuestionText: What is the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT)?
Options: A) A treaty banning nuclear weapons for all countries
B) A treaty allowing only existing nuclear states to keep weapons while stopping others from acquiring them
C) A treaty for the peaceful sharing of nuclear technology equally
D) A treaty eliminating all nuclear weapons by 2030
Topic: General Knowledge - World Affairs and Current Events
Explanation: NPT (Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty, 1968): three pillars: Non-proliferation (non-nuclear states won't develop nuclear weapons), Disarmament (nuclear states work toward eventual disarmament), Peaceful use (sharing civilian nuclear technology). Officially recognized 5 nuclear weapon states (P5): USA, USSR/Russia, UK, France, China. India, Pakistan, Israel, and North Korea are not NPT signatories. India conducted nuclear tests in 1974 (Pokhran I) and 1998 (Pokhran II — 'Shakti'). India has a 'No First Use' nuclear doctrine — won't use nuclear weapons first. India's civil nuclear deal with USA (2008) gave access to civilian nuclear technology outside NPT.

QuestionText: What is the Commonwealth of Nations?
Options: A) A group of 54 countries, most former British territories, promoting cooperation in trade, democracy, and development
B) A treaty organisation for English-speaking countries
C) Britain's economic zone including its territories
D) A military alliance of countries that were once part of the British Empire
Topic: General Knowledge - World Affairs and Current Events
Explanation: Commonwealth of Nations: 56 members (mainly former British territories), plus some nations with no British colonial history. Members: UK, India, Australia, Canada, New Zealand, South Africa, Singapore, Malaysia, Kenya, Nigeria, Pakistan, Bangladesh, etc. Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM): biennial. Commonwealth Games: held every 4 years (India hosted 2010, New Delhi). The British monarch was symbolic Head of the Commonwealth (now King Charles III). India is the most populous Commonwealth member. Membership is voluntary — Rwanda and Mozambique joined despite no British colonial history.

QuestionText: Which country is the largest producer of oil in the world?
Options: A) Saudi Arabia
B) Russia
C) USA
D) Iran
Topic: General Knowledge - World Affairs and Current Events
Explanation: USA is the world's largest oil producer (since 2018) due to the shale revolution (hydraulic fracturing/'fracking'). Producing ~12-13 million barrels/day. Saudi Arabia and Russia are 2nd and 3rd. OPEC (Organization of Petroleum Exporting Countries): 13 members including Saudi Arabia, UAE, Iraq, Iran, Venezuela — coordinate production to influence prices. OPEC+: OPEC + non-OPEC producers like Russia. India imports ~85% of its crude oil needs — major dependency. India is the world's 3rd largest oil consumer.

QuestionText: What is the Human Development Index (HDI)?
Options: A) A measure only of a country's GDP
B) A composite index measuring life expectancy, education, and per capita income to rank countries' human development
C) A military strength ranking index
D) A measure of a country's natural resource wealth
Topic: General Knowledge - World Affairs and Current Events
Explanation: HDI (Human Development Index): developed by Pakistani economist Mahbub ul Haq (with Amartya Sen) for UNDP. Published annually in Human Development Report. Three dimensions: long and healthy life (life expectancy), knowledge (education — mean years schooling, expected years schooling), decent standard of living (GNI per capita). Rankings: Norway, Switzerland, Iceland consistently top. India ranks around 132/191 (2021 HDR) — 'medium human development' category. HDI shows that high GDP alone doesn't equal high human development — social indicators matter.

QuestionText: What is SAARC?
Options: A) South African Alliance for Regional Cooperation
B) South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation — 8 nations of South Asia
C) Strategic Alliance for Asian Regional Competitiveness
D) Southeast Asian Association for Regional Cooperation
Topic: General Knowledge - World Affairs and Current Events
Explanation: SAARC (South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation): 8 member states — India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Nepal, Bhutan, Maldives, Afghanistan (suspended). Founded December 8, 1985 (Dhaka). Headquarters: Kathmandu, Nepal. Covers 3% of world's area, 21% of world's population. Largest member: India (population, economy). SAARC has struggled due to India-Pakistan tensions — summits often paralysed by bilateral disputes. SAFTA (South Asian Free Trade Area) exists but trade within SAARC is among the world's lowest for a major regional bloc. India focuses more on BIMSTEC as an alternative grouping.

QuestionText: What is the COP28 (2023) climate summit's significance?
Options: A) It was held in India
B) First global stocktake of Paris Agreement progress; historic agreement to transition away from fossil fuels
C) It established the Paris Agreement
D) It set a 2030 deadline for net-zero emissions for all countries
Topic: General Knowledge - World Affairs and Current Events
Explanation: COP28 (28th Conference of Parties, UNFCCC): held in Dubai, UAE (November-December 2023). Significance: First Global Stocktake (assessing progress since Paris Agreement 2015 — found insufficient). Historic decision: all countries agreed to 'transition away from fossil fuels' — first time fossil fuels directly named in a COP outcome. Loss and Damage Fund: operationalised to help vulnerable developing nations cope with climate disasters. UAE Consensus: commitment to triple renewables capacity and double energy efficiency by 2030. India's position: pushed for climate finance from developed nations, historical responsibility.

QuestionText: What is the Nobel Prize and in how many fields is it awarded?
Options: A) 4 fields
B) 5 fields
C) 6 fields
D) 7 fields
Topic: General Knowledge - World Affairs and Current Events
Explanation: Nobel Prizes: awarded annually since 1901. Founded by Swedish chemist Alfred Nobel (inventor of dynamite) per his will. 6 fields: Physics, Chemistry, Physiology or Medicine, Literature, Peace, Economic Sciences (added 1969 — technically the Sveriges Riksbank Prize). Awarded by Swedish Academy (Literature), Royal Swedish Academy (Physics, Chemistry, Economics), Karolinska Institutet (Medicine), Norwegian Nobel Committee (Peace). Prize: ~10 million Swedish kronor (~₹7 crore), gold medal, diploma. Most Nobel laureates: USA, UK, Germany. India: 12 laureates including Tagore, CV Raman, Mother Teresa, Amartya Sen, Abhijit Banerjee.

QuestionText: What is the 'Indo-Pacific' concept in international relations?
Options: A) A geographical term combining the Indian and Pacific Oceans as a strategic region
B) A new country formed by the merger of India and Pacific island nations
C) A military alliance of Pacific and Indian Ocean nations
D) An underwater mountain range connecting India to Pacific islands
Topic: General Knowledge - World Affairs and Current Events
Explanation: Indo-Pacific: strategic concept viewing the Indian Ocean and Pacific Ocean as an interconnected geopolitical space. Gained prominence post-2010s as China's influence grew. The region: covers 38 countries, 65% of world's population, ~62% of global GDP, half of global trade flows through it. QUAD (India, USA, Japan, Australia): promotes free and open Indo-Pacific. India's position: central to the Indo-Pacific due to its location, maritime capabilities, and strategic importance. Contrasts with China's preference for 'Asia-Pacific' framing (excluding India). India's Act East Policy aligns with Indo-Pacific strategy.

QuestionText: What was India's achievement at the Paris Olympics 2024?
Options: A) India topped the medal tally
B) India won 6 medals including a silver by Neeraj Chopra in javelin
C) India won its first gold medal in athletics
D) India won 10 medals for the first time
Topic: General Knowledge - World Affairs and Current Events
Explanation: Paris Olympics 2024 (July 26 - August 11): India won 6 medals. Neeraj Chopra: Silver in javelin throw (defending champion, won gold at Tokyo 2020). Manu Bhaker: Bronze in 10m air pistol (first Indian woman to win shooting medal at Olympics); also part of bronze-winning 10m air pistol mixed team. Swapnil Kusale: Bronze in 50m rifle 3 positions. Hockey: Men's team won Bronze (back-to-back bronze after Tokyo). Aman Sehrawat: Bronze in wrestling (57kg freestyle). India finished 71st in medal tally. Neeraj Chopra remains India's most celebrated track and field athlete.

QuestionText: What is the Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) number 4?
Options: A) No Poverty
B) Zero Hunger
C) Quality Education
D) Gender Equality
Topic: General Knowledge - World Affairs and Current Events
Explanation: SDG 4: Quality Education — 'Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all.' Targets: free primary and secondary education, equitable quality education, equal access to technical/vocational education and university, elimination of gender disparities. India's NEP (National Education Policy 2020) aims to align with SDG 4. SDG 1: No Poverty, SDG 2: Zero Hunger, SDG 3: Good Health, SDG 4: Quality Education, SDG 5: Gender Equality, SDG 13: Climate Action, SDG 16: Peace and Justice, SDG 17: Partnerships for Goals.

QuestionText: What is the IAEA?
Options: A) International Agricultural Economics Authority
B) International Atomic Energy Agency — promotes safe, secure peaceful use of nuclear technology
C) Indian Atomic Energy Alliance
D) International Aviation and Engineering Authority
Topic: General Knowledge - World Affairs and Current Events
Explanation: IAEA (International Atomic Energy Agency): established 1957, autonomous under UN. Headquarters: Vienna, Austria. Director General: Rafael Mariano Grossi (Argentina). Functions: promotes peaceful nuclear technology (power, medicine, agriculture, food safety), nuclear safeguards (verifying nuclear materials not diverted to weapons), nuclear safety (after Chernobyl 1986, Fukushima 2011). India-IAEA: India signed Additional Protocol allowing more intrusive inspections of civilian nuclear facilities as part of the 2008 India-US nuclear deal. Nobel Peace Prize 2005: awarded to IAEA and its then-DG Mohammed ElBaradei.

QuestionText: Which country has the world's largest coal reserves?
Options: A) China
B) India
C) USA
D) Russia
Topic: General Knowledge - World Affairs and Current Events
Explanation: USA has the world's largest proven coal reserves (approximately 248 billion tonnes — 23% of global reserves). Russia (2nd), Australia (3rd), China (4th), India (5th). However, China is the world's largest coal producer and consumer. India is the 2nd largest coal producer and importer. Global push for clean energy is reducing coal's role, but coal still generates ~35-40% of world's electricity. India aims to achieve 500 GW renewable energy capacity by 2030 to reduce coal dependence. Coal is central to India's energy security debate.

QuestionText: What is India's stance on the Russia-Ukraine war?
Options: A) India strongly supports Russia
B) India strongly condemned Russia and supports Ukraine
C) India maintains strategic autonomy — calling for dialogue while abstaining from UN votes condemning Russia
D) India has no official position
Topic: General Knowledge - World Affairs and Current Events
Explanation: Russia invaded Ukraine February 24, 2022. India's position: abstained from UN General Assembly resolutions condemning Russia (not opposing, not supporting). India called for immediate ceasefire, diplomatic solution, respect for UN Charter, territorial integrity. India continued buying discounted Russian oil (increased significantly after sanctions). Reasoning: India-Russia are longstanding partners (Russia supplies 60%+ of India's defence equipment); India doesn't want to alienate Russia toward China; strategic autonomy principle. PM Modi visited both Ukraine (2024) and Russia (2024) — first Indian PM visit to Ukraine since independence. Modi's message to Putin: 'This is not an era of war.'

QuestionText: What is the significance of Amrit Kaal in India's development?
Options: A) A traditional Indian festival celebrating 75 years
B) India's 25-year roadmap from 75th to 100th independence anniversary (2022-2047) for becoming a developed nation
C) A five-year economic plan similar to Soviet five-year plans
D) The period of India's highest agricultural production
Topic: General Knowledge - World Affairs and Current Events
Explanation: Amrit Kaal: India's 25-year vision period from 75th Independence Anniversary (2022) to 100th (2047 — 'India at 100' or 'Viksit Bharat 2047'). Goal: Transform India into a developed, self-reliant nation. Targets by 2047: GDP $30+ trillion (3rd largest), human development comparable to developed nations, modern infrastructure, digital economy, clean energy leader, strong defence manufacturing, elimination of poverty. PM Modi first used the term in the August 15, 2021 Independence Day speech. Union Budget 2022-23 and subsequent budgets framed around Amrit Kaal priorities.

QuestionText: Which country launched the world's first artificial satellite?
Options: A) USA
B) Germany
C) USSR (Soviet Union)
D) China
Topic: General Knowledge - World Affairs and Current Events
Explanation: The USSR (Soviet Union) launched Sputnik 1 on October 4, 1957 — the world's first artificial satellite, marking the beginning of the Space Age. This shocked the USA, triggering the Space Race. USA's first satellite: Explorer 1 (January 1958). First human in space: Yuri Gagarin (USSR, April 12, 1961 — World Space Day). First Moon landing: USA (Apollo 11, July 20, 1969 — Neil Armstrong, Buzz Aldrin). India's first satellite: Aryabhata (launched by USSR, April 19, 1975 — National Technology Day). India now has the world's 6th largest space programme.

QuestionText: What is the UNFCCC?
Options: A) United Nations Fiscal and Climate Change Convention
B) United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change — international treaty for addressing climate change
C) United Nations Fund for Carbon Credit Clearance
D) Universal Nuclear Fuel and Climate Containment Convention
Topic: General Knowledge - World Affairs and Current Events
Explanation: UNFCCC (United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change): international environmental treaty opened for signature at Earth Summit (Rio de Janeiro, 1992), entered into force 1994. 198 parties. Objective: stabilise greenhouse gas concentrations to prevent dangerous human interference with climate system. Annual COPs (Conference of Parties): major climate negotiations. Key outcomes: Kyoto Protocol (1997 — binding emission cuts for developed nations), Paris Agreement (2015 — all nations). Secretariat: Bonn, Germany. India is a party and actively participates in climate negotiations, pushing for climate finance and differentiated responsibilities for developed vs developing nations.

QuestionText: What does the abbreviation 'AI' stand for in the context of modern technology?
Options: A) Automated Information
B) Artificial Intelligence — machines simulating human cognitive functions
C) Advanced Internet
D) Automated Infrastructure
Topic: General Knowledge - World Affairs and Current Events
Explanation: AI (Artificial Intelligence): computer systems performing tasks that normally require human intelligence — learning, reasoning, problem-solving, perception, language understanding. Applications: ChatGPT (conversational AI), image recognition, autonomous vehicles, medical diagnosis, recommendation algorithms (Netflix, YouTube). India's National AI Strategy: NITI Aayog's #AIForAll initiative. India has a large AI talent pool and is a growing AI startup hub. AI raises important questions about: employment impact, privacy, bias in algorithms, and governance. India enacted its Digital Personal Data Protection Act (2023) partly in response to AI data challenges.
